notes: Customer: enterprise SaaS provider of support automation; strong agenda on ticket deflection and faster resolution
Primary ask: RAG pipeline for support agent + web self-service (deflection). Tight latency SLOs (95th <= 250ms) and top-5 quality for reranker.
Data profile: ~2.5M raw records (tickets, KB articles, community posts). After chunking ~10-15M passages. Expected growth 30% YoY.
Traffic profile: baseline 8-12 QPS, expected sustained 10k queries/day, nightly batch reindexing window; burst to 40-60 QPS during incidents.
Indexing asks: incremental upserts, real-time rank refresh for high-priority articles, retention policy for GDPR-sensitive content.
Quality metrics they care about: recall@5 > 0.85 (retriever), reranker precision@5 >= 0.78, ticket deflection delta >= 20% headroom.
Latency constraints: full end-to-end RAG (retrieve + rerank + model answer) needs to meet 95p <= 250ms for agent UX; acceptable to fall back to faster model or cached answers during breaches.
Cost sensitivity: target infra cost per query < $0.03 across typical traffic. Concerned about cross-encoder reranker cost at scale.
Model preferences: open-model embeddings (1536-d) for cost predictability; interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization + batching.
Security: must support SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, KMS key control for private deployment; legal requires documented data residency (EU subset for EU customers).
Integrations: Zendesk + Salesforce primarily; wants one-click connector and event hooks for upserts on ticket resolves.
Quotes / call notes: 'We will buy if you can prove stable 95p at 250ms with reranker in the loop and keep cost under the target.' — Head of Product (E. Morales).

POC findings: basic ANN retrieval (FAISS/HNSW) gave fast recall but inconsistent top-5 relevance; cross-encoder reranker fixes relevance but added latency. SE proposed hybrid: first-pass cheap retriever + small cross-encoder on top-10 candidates + caching top answers for high-frequency queries.

Recommended Redwood levers discussed: grouping by customer intent to prefetch vectors, prefix KV caching for agent sessions, dynamic routing to cheaper model variants under load, and optimized quantized embeddings to reduce storage + cost.
Open legal items: formal statement on where vectors/live copies are stored and deletion SLA for EU-resident user data (linked to SEC-9210).
Decision criteria: 1) meet latency SLA with reranker, 2) clear cost per query model, 3) VPC/private deployment option or dedicated pods, 4) integration effort under 4 engineering sprints.
Next asks from customer: scale test with 10M passage index, two-tier rerank A/B (full cross-encoder vs distilled reranker), and written dedicated pricing with burst SLAs.
